eligibility.reason: The primary paper reports the North Carolina High School Athletic Injury Study, a prospective cohort sampled from 100 North Carolina public high schools. Trained school contacts collected study-specific injury reports and weekly participation forms from 1996 to 1999. It is not High School RIO, NCAA surveillance, NATION/Datalys, or another national US surveillance feed.
eligibility.footballSubset: Boys' soccer and girls' soccer rows only. American football and the other ten sports are excluded from this extraction.

studyDetails.leadAuthor.sourceQuote: Sarah B. Knowles, Stephen W. Marshall, J. Michael Bowling, Dana Loomis, Robert Millikan, Jinzhen Yang, Nancy L. Weaver, William Kalsbeek, and Frederick O. Mueller

studyDetails.title.sourceQuote: A Prospective Study of Injury Incidence among North Carolina High School Athletes

studyDetails.studyDesign.sourceQuote: The North Carolina High School Athletic Injury Study was a prospective cohort study conducted from 1996 to 1999.

participantCharacteristics.fifaDisciplin.sourceQuote: Twelve sports were included: boys' and girls' soccer, boys' and girls' track, boys' and girls' basketball, baseball, softball, wrestling, volleyball, cheerleading, and football.

participantCharacteristics.country.sourceQuote: injury and risk factor data were collected from a sample of high school varsity athletes from 100 public high schools in North Carolina

participantCharacteristics.levelOfPlay.sourceQuote: all varsity athletes playing any of these selected sports were included as participants

definitions.injuryDefinition.sourceQuote: A reportable injury was one that resulted from participation in a high school sport and either limited the student's full participation in the sport the day following the injury or required medical attention by a medical professional. Additionally, concussions, fractures, or eye injuries were reportable regardless of whether they resulted in lost participation or required medical attention.

definitions.incidenceDefinition.sourceQuote: Incidence rates were estimated as the number of injuries divided by the sum of athlete-exposures. The analysis of incidence rates included only injuries and exposure time during the preseason and regular season.

definitions.mechanismReporting.sourceQuote: Most school contacts were the athletic trainer (69.0 percent), with the remainder being athletic directors (31.0 percent). Data collectors were trained to administer the data collection instruments.

exposure.numberOfSeasons.sourceQuote: A prospective cohort study of injury risk factors was conducted from 1996 to 1999

exposure.exposureMeasurementUnit.sourceQuote: An 'athlete-exposure' is one athlete participating in one practice or competition.

injuryOutcome.injuryIncidenceOverall.sourceQuote: Boys' soccer 2.81; Girls' soccer 2.35 per 1,000 athlete-exposures

injuryOutcome.injuryIncidenceCi95.sourceQuote: Boys' soccer 95% CI 2.03, 3.90; Girls' soccer 95% CI 1.55, 3.55
